name: Lindab International AB
reason: Swedish steel ventilation/building products maker whose adjusted EPS of SEK 9.63 (2025) is still below the 2022 peak of 12.70 (5y CAGR 2.1%), with an EBIT margin of 7.6% vs a 13.2% max and net debt/EBITDA of 2.45x; construction-cyclical and ordinary, with no specialness.

name: Buzzi SpA
reason: Cement producer whose EPS quadrupled to EUR 4.93 (0.96x its 10y max) as the EBIT margin rose from 8.5% to 18.9% (82nd pctile), while consensus implies only ~6%/yr; near-peak, energy- and construction-cycle-driven earnings with large USD exposure, matching the US CRH/EXP precedent.

name: Hemnet Group AB
reason: Dominant Swedish property portal with a 44% EBIT margin and EPS up from SEK 0.21 to 5.49 (2020-25) through price increases, but EPS is 1.0x its peak and consensus FY1 is -30.6%, which signals a competitive and pricing challenge to the moat; the record since 2018 is too short to forecast 10 years out.

name: Neurones SA
reason: Founder-run, net-cash French IT services firm with a steady record (adjusted EPS EUR 0.89 to 2.14, 9.1% 10y CAGR, worst year -1.7%), but EPS has stalled since 2023 at EUR 2.13-2.16 with the EBIT margin down from 10.7% to 8.4%, and the labour-based service desk/infrastructure outsourcing model faces a credible 5-yr AI-automation threat.

name: Implenia AG
reason: Swiss construction contractor with a 1.4% average 10y EBIT margin, a 2020 loss (EPS CHF -7.30), negative 10y FCF conversion and revenue CAGR of 0.6%; a low-margin, project-risk business with no specialness.

name: Sanlorenzo SpA
reason: High-end yacht builder with good returns (ROIC 19.8%) and EPS tripling to EUR 2.99 (2020-25), but EPS is at its peak, consensus slows to ~3%/yr, FCF conversion is only 0.55, and demand depends on the luxury/UHNW wealth cycle; this cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Michelin (CGEM SCA)
reason: Tyre maker with adjusted EPS of EUR 2.36 in 2025, barely above the 2016 level of 2.20 (10y CAGR 3.2%, 3/10 years >=7%), and an EBIT margin of 10.2% at the 18th pctile under Asian competition and auto-volume cyclicality; a good franchise with no route to 7%.

name: Südzucker AG
reason: Sugar/bioethanol producer whose earnings follow EU sugar and ethanol prices: EPS swung from EUR 2.81 (FY2023) to -2.05 (FY2025), with a 10y average ROIC of -0.4% and net debt/EBITDA of 6.2x; commodity-driven and controlled by a beet-grower cooperative.

name: Einhell Germany AG
reason: Family-controlled DIY power-tool and garden brand with Asian-sourced products; EPS rose to EUR 6.75 (1.0x its peak, margin 82nd pctile), but FCF conversion is only 0.4 because of working capital, and it competes as a value player against Bosch, TTI and Makita; cheap but ordinary consumer-cyclical with no durable moat.

name: Enel SpA
reason: Italian state-influenced (MEF ~24%) integrated utility with adjusted EPS of EUR 0.69 vs an adjusted/GAAP gap of 36%, net debt/EBITDA of 3.9x, 10y ROIC of 4.3% and consensus growth of 4-6%/yr; regulated and policy-set returns with no >=7% route.

name: Zabka Group SA
reason: Polish convenience-store leader with a franchise model, EPS up from PLN 0.35 to 1.10 (2023-25) and consensus of 22-26%, but it has been public only since 2025 after a sponsor exit, carries net debt/EBITDA of 2.2x and trades at 21x NTM; the record is too short and untested in a downturn to forecast with confidence.

name: Pepco Group NV
reason: Discount variety retailer in restructuring (Poundland exit) with GAAP EPS swinging EUR 0.30 / 0.18 / -1.29 / 0.29 (2022-25), a 10y ROIC of 2.3%, and only 1/5 years of >=7% growth; a turnaround with no proven per-share record.

name: Forbo Holding AG
reason: Linoleum flooring and conveyor-belt maker whose EPS fell from CHF 93.49 (2021) to 49.46 (2025; 10y CAGR -2.4%) despite buybacks, with the EBIT margin down from 15.1% to 8.4% (9th pctile) on weak construction volumes; no growth route.

name: Imerys SA
reason: Industrial minerals producer with adjusted EPS down from EUR 4.78 (2017) to 1.73 (2025; 10y CAGR -8.3%), a 10y ROIC of 1.1%, a 130% adjusted/GAAP gap and net debt/EBITDA of 2.6x; commodity-cyclical and in structural decline.

name: Cyfrowy Polsat SA
reason: Polish pay-TV/telecom/media conglomerate that diversified into green energy and real estate; EPS fell to PLN -2.98 (2025), the EBIT margin fell from 19.9% to 9.6%, net debt/EBITDA is 3.9x, and a founder-family control dispute is under way; governance and capital allocation fail.

name: Electrolux Professional AB
reason: Commercial kitchen and laundry equipment maker whose EPS of SEK 2.56 (2025) is still below the 2017 level of 2.96, with an EBIT margin of 8.3% vs 13.6% and growth bought (acq/FCF 0.74); a decent installed base but no organic >=7% route.

name: Drägerwerk AG & Co. KGaA
reason: Medical and safety equipment maker with volatile EPS (EUR 12.32 in the 2020 pandemic, -3.47 in 2022, 7.47 in 2025), a 5% average EBIT margin and a 5.6% 10y ROIC; thin, unpredictable economics despite a family-controlled franchise.

name: Kontron AG
reason: Austrian IoT/embedded-hardware roll-up with acq/FCF of 1.21, shares growing 3.7%/yr, a 4.4% average EBIT margin and EPS of EUR 2.19 (2025) below the 2022 peak of 3.64; growth comes from acquisitions, and the hardware economics are ordinary.

name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals Plc
reason: Generic injectables/oral Rx/MENA branded generics maker whose USD-reported adjusted EPS grew only 4.7%/yr over 10y (USD 1.42 to 2.26), with a 69% adjusted/GAAP gap, an EBIT margin of 17% (18th pctile) and earnings set by US generic pricing and tariffs; no forecastable >=7% route.

name: ISS A/S
reason: Low-margin facility services contractor (10y average EBIT 3.7%) with adjusted EPS of DKK 15.4 in 2025, flat vs 14.62 in 2015, after a 2020 loss and contract write-downs, plus a 123% adjusted/GAAP gap; a labour-intensive business with no moat.
